My Name is Reeva

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A new documentary unveils the loss of the Steenkamp family

Unique Selling Point:
The Oscar Pistorius trial drew media attention from around the world, witness testimonies, cross examination, expert evidence were all under scrutiny as the court tried to ascertain the events that led to Reeva Steenkamp's death. As each layer of the case was unfolding, Reeva Steenkamp's parents, grief stricken, listened intently trying to piece together the last moments of their daughter's life. The documentary,shifts attention from the athlete's fall from grace and the gruesome detail of the Reeva's murder to the Steenkamp family's life after suffering a tragic loss. Interviews leading up to Barry Steenkamp meeting with Oscar, for the victim offender dialogue process, reveal a broken man. His burly figure is deceptive, his eyes are sorrowful and his face heavy with grief.

Director, Warren Batchelor, who was present for the dialogue between Steenkamp and Pistorius, will describe the emotion of the moment. The insert will scrutinise if this process, which is meant to offer closure for families and help them move on, does indeed lay the groundwork for that.


Summary:
The documentary re-visits different elements of the Oscar Pistorius trial, experts share insights into witness and expert testimonies as well as evidence. Crime scene analysts poke holes into Pistorius's version of events and re-enactments are used to illustrate poignant details that were heard in court. Desperate for answers, the expert technical detail addresses how a murder may have occurred but many families much like the Steenkamps want to know why. In the documentary we learn that over the years Barry and June Steenkamp, are still haunted by the question, why Oscar Pistorius killed Reeva.

Using excerpts of the documentary and interview with director Warren Batchelor and an expert psychologist, the insert will grapple with the notion of closure this family has been looking for.

Script:


It made headlines around the world on Valentine's Day 2013. Paralympic superstar, Oscar Pistorious, shot and killed his model girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp.

The trial that followed, attracted global media attention.


And as horrific details of Reeva’s final moments emerged in court, her parents, June and Barry, were visibly traumatised.

A distraught mother and father, re-living their loss.


Barry Steenkamp Testimony in court during trial.

I just don’t wish that on anybody in the whole world.
Now, a three part documentary series provides an intimate portrait of a young life lost: doting daughter, dedicated friend, ambitious model - Reeva Rebeca Steenkamp.

June (in documentary)
Barry picked me up when Reeva was born, we were leaving the hospital in a kombi with about five dogs in, the favourite ones came to the hospital to pick her up. We were so excited, we were so enthralled.



Memories of happier times are an antidote to the pain of losing their daughter. But, as the film unfolds, it’s clear June and Barry bear unhealed wounds.

June (in documentary)
Death defines me now, her death. It does define me, I’m not the same person.
The film is the result of a 7-year relationship between June and Barry and director, Warren Batchelor. Having gained their trust, he went on to film interviews with some of Reeva’s loved ones and closest friends.
Warren Batchelor
I’ve got so many people that have talked to me about her, who gave me all these insights into her personality.
Weaving the interviews and reflections together, fell to head writer, Justin Strydom. Perhaps his most difficult task, deciphering the concept of forgiveness and what it means to the Steenkamps - now in their late 70s.
Justin Strydom

Everybody knows that Barry and June said they forgive Oscar, but saying that you forgive somebody and then living that truth or that reality I think was very different for Barry and June. I think, you don’t, I don’t even think they knew how difficult it was going to be.

June (in documentary)

It’s difficult now, you know, we both were grieving all this time and it’s, it’s actually ruined our lives not having her. So that, it’s ruined our marriage as well.
How could they have predicted, for example, that one day they’d be asked to meet the man who killed their daughter?

The department of Correctional Services runs a programme called The Victim Offender Dialogue or VOD.


The invitation to meet Oscar as part of the VOD process was delivered to June and Barry by their longtime lawyer, Tanya Koen.

Tanya Koen (in documentary)

Today I had to do one of the most difficult things I’ve had to do in my career. I had to bring a letter to June and Barry, written by Oscar Pistorious.
Once eligible for parole, prisoners request a meeting with their victims or their families to convey their remorse and ask for forgiveness. Now up for parole after serving half of his sentence, that’s what Oscar has done.

Warren Batchelor
This is not sensationalism, this is a human story. About two people’s journey, old wounds have opened up again, they’ve had to relive it again. And June’s journey on this was a very difficult one.

June (in documentary)

I don’t want to see him again ever, I would have been feeling ill, and afraid, I don’t know why afraid.
Barry feels differently: still distressed and living with a heart condition, he’s agreed to the meeting.


In the documentary, he describes getting advice from a psychologist.

Barry (in documentary)
She says as a professional I would tell you not to go, I said if it were your daughter, what would you do, she said then I would go.
Warren Batchelor
It was a very emotional day for Barry, he went through with it and he faced his daughter’s killer.

Barry (in doccie)
You don’t know what to expect but it’s a very worrying couple of days
Masa - Justin the documentary is a three part series, what’s the narrative that holds it together
Justin Strydom
The first one is really the VOD process the other important part of the story which is who Reeva was. And then the other part of it is obviously what happened on that night, those three stories are really linked by one idea and that’s Reeva.
